arxiv-2102-13003.title: An introduction to distributed training of deep neural networks for segmentation tasks with large seismic datasets
arxiv-2102-13003.creator: Claire Birnie, Haithem Jarraya, Fredrik Hansteen
arxiv-2102-13003.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Claire Birnie, Haithem Jarraya, Fredrik Hansteen. Deep learning applications are drastically progressing in seismic processing and interpretation tasks. However, the majority of approaches subsample data volumes and restrict model sizes to minimise computational requirements. Subsampling the data risks losing vital spatio-temporal information which could aid training whilst restricting model sizes can impact model performance, or in some extreme cases, renders more complicated tasks such as segmentation impossible.

arxiv-2109-09858.title: Intensionalizing Abstract Meaning Representations: Non-Veridicality and Scope
arxiv-2109-09858.creator: Gregor Williamson, Patrick Elliott, Yuxin Ji, Jinho D. Choi
arxiv-2109-09858.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gregor Williamson, Patrick Elliott, Yuxin Ji, Jinho D. Choi. Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) is a graphical meaning representation language designed to represent propositional information about argument structure. However, at present it is unable to satisfyingly represent non-veridical intensional contexts, often licensing inappropriate inferences. In this paper, we show how to resolve the problem of non-veridicality without appealing to layered graphs through a mapping from AMRs into Simply-Typed Lambda Calculus (STLC).

arxiv-2112-08941.title: Relationship Between the Prime-Counting Function and a Unique Prime Number Sequence
arxiv-2112-08941.creator: Michael P. May
arxiv-2112-08941.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Michael P. May. In mathematics, the prime counting function π ⁡ ( x ) \pi(x) is defined as the function yielding the number of primes less than or equal to a given number x x . In this paper, we prove that the asymptotic limit of a summation operation performed on a unique subsequence of the prime numbers yields the prime number counting function π ⁡ ( x ) \pi(x) as x x approaches ∞ \infty .

arxiv-2206-07979.title: Towards Positive Geometries of Massive Scalar field theories
arxiv-2206-07979.creator: Alok Laddha
arxiv-2206-07979.description: Abstract Building on the prior work in [ 1 ] we locate a family of positive geometries in the kinematic space which are a specific class of convex realisations of the associahedron. These realisations are obtained by scaling and translating the kinematic space associahedron discovered by by Arkani-Hamed, Bai, He and Yan (ABHY).

arxiv-2208-02112.title: Various bounds on the minimum number of arcs in a k k -dicritical digraph
arxiv-2208-02112.creator: Pierre Aboulker, Quentin Vermande
arxiv-2208-02112.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Pierre Aboulker, Quentin Vermande. The dichromatic number χ → ​ ( G ) \vec{\chi}(G) of a digraph G G is the least integer k k such that G G can be partitioned into k k acyclic digraphs. A digraph is k k -dicritical if χ → ​ ( G ) = k \vec{\chi}(G)=k and each proper subgraph H H of G G satisfies χ → ​ ( H ) ≤ k − 1 \vec{\chi}(H)\leq k-1 .

arxiv-2306-02281.title: Theory of exciton-polariton condensation in gap-confined eigenmodes
arxiv-2306-02281.creator: Davide Nigro, Dario Gerace
arxiv-2306-02281.description: Abstract Exciton-polaritons are bosonic-like elementary excitations in semiconductors, which have been recently shown to display large occupancy of topologically protected polariton bound states in the continuum in suitably engineered photonic lattices [Nature 605 , 447 (2022)], compatible with the definition of polariton condensation.

arxiv-2410-12400.title: QUIDS: Query Intent Description for Exploratory Search via Dual Space Modeling
arxiv-2410-12400.creator: Yumeng Wang, Xiuying Chen, Suzan Verberne
arxiv-2410-12400.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yumeng Wang, Xiuying Chen, Suzan Verberne. In exploratory search, users often submit vague queries to investigate unfamiliar topics, but receive limited feedback about how the search engine understood their input. This leads to a self-reinforcing cycle of mismatched results and trial-and-error reformulation. To address this, we study the task of generating user-facing natural language query intent descriptions that surface what the system likely inferred the query to mean, based on post-retrieval evidence.

arxiv-2505-00835.title: Multi-site modelling and reconstruction of past extreme skew surges along the French Atlantic coast
arxiv-2505-00835.creator: Nathan Huet, Philippe Naveau, Anne Sabourin
arxiv-2505-00835.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nathan Huet, Philippe Naveau, Anne Sabourin. Appropriate modelling of extreme skew surges is crucial, particularly for coastal risk management. Our study focuses on modelling extreme skew surges along the French Atlantic coast, with a particular emphasis on investigating the extremal dependence structure between stations. We employ the peak-over-threshold framework, where a multivariate extreme event is defined whenever at least one location records a large value, though not necessarily all stations simultaneously.

arxiv-2509-09384.title: Taking the Highway or the Green Road? Conditional Temperature Forecasts Under Alternative SSP Scenarios
arxiv-2509-09384.creator: Anthoulla Phella, Vasco J. Gabriel, Luis F. Martins
arxiv-2509-09384.description: Abstract In this paper, using the Bayesian VAR framework suggested by Chan et al., 2025 , we produce conditional temperature forecasts up until 2050, by exploiting both equality and inequality constraints on climate drivers like carbon dioxide or methane emissions.

arxiv-2512-02554.title: OmniPerson: Unified Identity-Preserving Pedestrian Generation
arxiv-2512-02554.creator: Changxiao Ma, Chao Yuan, Xincheng Shi, Yuzhuo Ma, Yongfei Zhang, Longkun Zhou, Yujia Zhang, Shangze Li, Yifan Xu
arxiv-2512-02554.description: Abstract Person re-identification (ReID) suffers from a lack of large-scale high-quality training data due to challenges in data privacy and annotation costs. While previous approaches have explored pedestrian generation for data augmentation, they often fail to ensure identity consistency and suffer from insufficient controllability, thereby limiting their effectiveness in dataset augmentation.

pmc-12470838.creator: Hye Kyung Jeon, Gwang Ha Kim, Vincenzo Davide Palumbo
pmc-12470838.description: Gastric subepithelial tumors (SETs) are commonly identified during routine endoscopy. Most SETs are asymptomatic and small (<2 cm) and exhibit benign behavior over time. pmc-12549679.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveThis study aimed to compare the effects of five post-exercise recovery interventions—massage, cold-water immersion (CWI), vibration therapy, functional electrical stimulation (FES), and static stretching—on central nervous modulation, neuromuscular function recovery, and inflammatory response following exercise-induced muscle fatigue (EIMF).MethodsThis randomized controlled trial employed a two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA; group × time) to evaluate the effects of different recovery interventions over time.

pmc-12709761.title: Whole exome sequencing in pediatric hyperammonemia: significant diagnostic yield and identification of three novel variants
pmc-12709761.creator: Reza Hajati, Fatemeh Hashemian, Shadab Salehpour, Arezou Sayad
pmc-12709761.description: BackgroundHyperammonemia, not a disorder, but an outcome of a disorder marked by elevated ammonia levels in the blood, is a serious medical condition that makes accurate diagnosis based on clinical and laboratory findings challenging. In this scenario, employing advanced genetic tests like whole exome sequencing can provide crucial insights that help clinicians better manage the disease.

pmc-12751508.title: Plasma IL-6 level predict the risk of in-hospital mortality in HIV-associated pneumocystis pneumonia
pmc-12751508.creator: Huan Xia, Jing Song, Yue Hu, Lei Li, Liying Gao, Ping Ma
pmc-12751508.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe study aimed to determine plasma immune-inflammatory biomarkers that may predict in-hospital mortality in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-infected individuals diagnosed with pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP).MethodsThis study prospectively included 125 antiretroviral therapy (ART)-naïve, HIV-infected patients with PCP. Biomarkers involving clinical variables and 8 pre-selected plasma inflammatory cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12, IL-17, TNF-α, and IFN-γ) were evaluated at time of admission. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify factors substantially associated with in-hospital mortality.

pmc-12756394.description: Weight cycling (WC), defined as the repeated process of weight gain and loss, is one of the biggest challenges in the management of weight. pmc-13062418.description: Introduction:Femoral neck fractures in lower limb amputees are uncommon. We report the case of a 55-year-old woman with a femoral neck fracture and an ipsilateral below-knee amputation (BKA), managed with hemiarthroplasty.

pmc-13638280.title: On the optimal sodium correction rate in hyponatraemia and clinical outcome: a meta-analysis
